competitor_mentions.quote: We evaluated Storsund BI briefly last year and one thing that stood out was their bulk seat import via CSV.

narrative: Four routine how-to tickets over five months, all resolved within a week, covering seats, report builder and exports. The Storsund BI mention is a passing feature comparison from over a year ago, not active shopping. This is a healthy, low-touch account.

Six tickets over a year, every one a straightforward configuration question (refresh frequency, tile resizing, recipient limits, filenames), each closed in two to four days with no complaint language anywhere. No sign of friction or disengagement.

A rolling series of connector/export/dashboard/API faults since October 2024 keeps recurring despite being logged as resolved each time: the export job's silent-failure bug reappears in July 2025 with the customer noting it is the "same silent-failure pattern as back in October" (nine months earlier), and dashboard staleness recurs three separate times between January and April 2025 ("Third dashboard issue since January"). Tone stays factual rather than angry throughout, but the breadth of modules affected and the lack of a durable fix for either core thread is a real reliability concern.

Only three tickets in four months, but both substantive ones show the quiet-erosion pattern: alert thresholds resetting on every sync led the team to just "check the raw figures in Excel first thing instead of waiting on the alerts," and stale currency rates on the consolidation dashboard led to a "manual rate-check step" built into month-end close, with the customer noting "there's no immediate pressure." Neither fix is confirmed working afterward — this is an account routing around unresolved problems rather than pushing for real ones.

Alerts were unreliable for nearly a year (April 2024 to June 2025) despite two explicit escalation requests, at one point prompting "We need to know if this is fixable or if we should be planning around it." The June 2025 escalation produced a real fix, confirmed across three subsequent calm, positive tickets through August (API, connector, dashboard, all routine feature questions). This is a recovered account, not a currently at-risk one.

Enterprise account with a genuinely rough start to 2025 — seat delays, a month-long report builder outage, and an explicit escalation demand in April ("the pattern of slow fixes is a real concern") that went unanswered for over a week. Since a July account-team call, tickets are calm and routine ("things have felt more responsive since," "no rush") through September. Recovered, with the escalation clearly having landed.
Five widely-spaced how-to tickets over 12 months (API auth, exports, templates, permissions, connectors), all resolved in two to four days with no complaint language. Straightforward healthy account.
Seven feature-question tickets over a year, all resolved within a week, none touching on any recurring fault. A textbook healthy, low-friction relationship.

A dashboard/connector refresh bug reported in March 2025 recurred within days and was still present by June, with the customer settling into a manual Excel double-check workaround and downgrading the request to "flagging mainly for the record rather than asking it to jump the queue." That is resignation language, not resolution, even though every ticket is marked resolved.

Seven tickets over ten months, all setup and configuration questions tied to onboarding a subsidiary (connectors, alerts, API scoping), resolved promptly with consistently professional, unremarkable tone. Healthy account expanding its footprint.

competitor_mentions.quote: As part of our operations tooling review this year we've also had a look at Storsund BI, partly prompted by these kinds of formatting issues recurring across a few modules.

Storsund BI's team demoed a comparable connector setup for us last week as part of the review, and it was useful to see how another platform handles retry and backoff, for context if it helps your side too.

We're still finalising our tooling review, with Storsund BI among the options being considered, but no decision has been made and this seat change is really just about matching usage to what we actually need right now.

narrative: API/connector timeouts grew from roughly one-in-five calls in December 2024 to one-in-three by May 2025, alongside export formatting corruption and dashboard load times rising from a couple of seconds to 15-20 seconds. The account has now cut two seats at renewal citing "recurring connector and dashboard slowness this year," and Storsund BI has gone from a passing comparison to a formal demo to "among the options being considered" in an active tooling review across three separate tickets. Quiet disengagement, not anger — and the more dangerous kind.
A single, simple export configuration question, resolved in four days. No history to judge risk from beyond this one clean interaction.

Over seven months this formally-worded but increasingly pointed account logged four recurring-reliability threads: connector failures (three instances, "each one has taken a week or more to resolve"), exports failing three times in July alone, a dashboard the team has "stopped trusting," and a December SSO attribute-mapping question that was simply never picked back up (still marked unresolved). The final ticket (22 July) ties the latest connector timeout directly to January and March and asks "whether this is going to keep coming back" — controlled tone, but visibly out of patience, with an open reliability question left hanging at the end of the log.

competitor_mentions.quote: We looked briefly at Dashlume's alerting model for comparison and their approach seemed more flexible on this point, so keen to understand what's possible here too.
We're still evaluating Dashlume as part of a broader review this year, but this particular workaround has taken the pressure off in the meantime.

narrative: A token-lifetime bug (docs said 24 hours, actual was roughly two) caused failed overnight finance-close jobs in April 2024. Rather than get a working fix or failure-alert from Kataja, the customer built its own external monitoring script by July, declaring "no urgency on the original token or alert questions from our side anymore" — that is disengagement from the platform for this function, not resolution by it. They are also "still evaluating Dashlume as part of a broader review," a procurement-context competitor mention sitting on top of an issue Kataja never actually closed.

A February 2025 API breakage (401 errors after a platform update, "disrupting an automated reporting process... for 15 internal stakeholders") was never resolved, and by August the customer notes it "was also never fully explained to us. We are still working around it in some cases." Alerts then failed three separate times across the year, each described in escalating terms ("I need it fixed today"), and the final, unresolved ticket states the monitoring team "has stopped relying on the alert system at this point because it cannot be trusted" and calls it "an infrastructure reliability issue." This account is failing openly, with two live unresolved threads at the end.

Within a ten-week span (December 2024-February 2025) this account logged problems across connectors, exports, alerts and dashboards, several of which recurred after being marked resolved: the MySQL SSL fix "did not hold" a month later, and alert delivery had "never been fully resolved" since December despite three separate tickets on it. The customer explicitly tracked the pattern ("This is the fifth separate issue we have raised since December. At what point does this get escalated?") and closed the batch asking whether there is "a systemic issue with our account configuration" — a customer with concrete, compounding evidence and an exhausted tone.

Accumulating dashboard/API/alert failures through 2024 culminated in an explicit escalation demand in January 2025 ("fourth issue overall since June... I want this escalated"), which produced a spring "escalation call" after which the account reports sustained stability across five subsequent months of tickets (June-October), including several low-stakes routine questions. Recovered account, currently healthy.

Roughly a year of near-monthly failures (API, connectors, exports, alerts twice, dashboards) culminated in a January 2025 escalation ("almost one a month... We need a real fix, not another ticket"), and every ticket since April 2025 has been calm and increasingly exploratory — stability check-ins and feature requests ("given how stable things have been, would it be worth adding..."). One trivial cosmetic filename-format complaint remains open, but this reads as a fully recovered, actively engaged account.

A genuinely rough 2024: wrong numbers reaching management (April), an undocumented breaking API change that cost "two days of lost pipeline output" (May), and a third distinct report-delivery failure that led the team to abandon scheduled reports for manual exports every morning. By September, however, tickets are markedly calmer and resolve faster (one and four days versus 17-20 days mid-year, "not blocking us, worth flagging"), and the recurring Report Builder quality complaint ("each fix seems to introduce a new one") has no further instance after June. Cooling off, not currently at crisis pitch.

competitor_mentions.quote: we had a look at Dashlume this month as part of a general review of reporting tools, mainly prompted by wanting more visibility into sync reliability generally.
Still keeping half an eye on Dashlume as part of our review, though nothing decided yet.

narrative: Only three tickets over four months, but the content is the quiet-erosion pattern: intermittent connector failures (October) and export staleness (December) that the customer now attributes to "the same underlying reliability question," a workaround that has "become part of our routine," and an active, reliability-driven review of Dashlume mentioned in both later tickets. Low volume is not health here — the underlying issue was never actually fixed and a competitor evaluation is live.
